<!-- generated by `azelf init` — edit freely; init will not overwrite a file it did not write -->

Run the azelf dispatcher from the MAIN checkout. One ticket, one worktree, one session.

## Always start with the plan

```sh
bunx azelf run --plan
```

This opens nothing. It prints the ready tickets grouped into waves by their blocking
edges, and — this is the part worth reading — the reason each excluded ticket cannot
run yet. If a ticket you expected is missing, the answer is in that output, not in the
config.

Tickets are picked up only when they carry the ready label AND have no open blockers.

They always come from **the repo you are standing in** — `gh` resolves the owner and
name from the git remote of the working directory, so there is nothing to configure
and no way for one repo's tickets to leak into another's run. The ticket body is then
written to `.slice-ticket.md` inside each prepped worktree, so a session reads a local
file rather than making a network call.

## Then dispatch

```sh
bunx azelf run 12 14      # prep and open exactly these
bunx azelf run            # the whole first wave
bunx azelf run --auto     # dispatch, then land each slice as it finishes
```

Each ticket gets a git worktree outside the repo, its ticket text written to
`.slice-ticket.md` inside it, and a session opened there. `--auto` implies
`--self-land`: the session marks itself done and the dispatcher lands it.

## The dispatcher re-runs the gates itself

Do not skip a gate because a session reported it green. That is deliberate and it is
the whole reason landing is a separate step — an agent can leave a branch committed,
clean and gate-green while the ticket is half-built. Every gate is read-only, and the
runner checks `git status` after each one and fails the land by name if a gate wrote
anything.

## What to watch for

**Do not dispatch tickets that modify the dispatcher through `--auto` in the tree
they will land into.** The tool that lands slice N is the tool slice N−1 just
changed. Run those serially, from the main tree, with no other slices open.

**A slice that will not land is PARKED, and you are asked what to do.** The four
failure paths — a failed rebase, red gates, a `VERDICT: BLOCK` spec review, or
`slice-land.sh` refusing — all stop and offer: retry now, land anyway without the
review, park it, or stop the run. Non-interactive runs park automatically.

A parked slice is retried when, and only when, its branch moves. That is the point:
a review verdict on an unchanged diff cannot change, so re-running it is a paid loop
rather than optimism. Go commit a fix in the worktree and the next round picks it up
by itself.

If every open slice is parked and nothing is running, the dispatcher says so and
stops instead of sleeping in a circle. The run ends with a list of what is parked and
why, and exits non-zero.

**A session that never comes up** is reported after the launch grace window. The
report names the launcher, because that is the thing to look at: `warp` starts
sessions through a shell hook and a marker file, everything else carries the command
itself.

## Landing by hand

```sh
./scripts/slice-land.sh 12    # from the main worktree; fast-forward only
```
